releasedVersion.description: A specific released version only -- not 'main'. Used where the value must be a fixed baseline comparable against future releases (see last_checked_version below), unlike version_added/version_deprecated/version_removed where 'main' legitimately means 'happened on the dev branch, not yet released'.

versionAdded.description: 'X.Y.Z' = known first version. '≤X.Y.Z' = present as of that release, earlier releases not checked (a lower bound, mdn/browser-compat-data style). 'main' = dev branch only. false = not supported. null = not yet evaluated. 'not-applicable' = doesn't apply here (commands only -- scripts/validate.py rejects it on messages/enums).

subStatement.description: One support statement: a single version range (version_added up to version_removed, if any), plus how it was established. 'basis' is optional here -- used directly for a command frame's params, sentinel subfeatures and mav_frames.rejects_unsupported, where an omitted basis means 'same basis as the enclosing frame' (a documentation convention scripts/validate.py permits but doesn't resolve). version_deprecated/version_removed only valid when version_added is a real version; last_checked_version not valid alongside version_removed -- both enforced by scripts/validate.py.

statement.description: subStatement with 'basis' required -- used for messages/enums and each command frame's own 'supported'.

statementOrHistory.description: A single statement, or a history array of them (newest first, non-overlapping) for an added -> removed -> re-added timeline. In an array every entry must have a real version_added -- ordering/overlap checked by scripts/validate.py.

compatibility.description: Object keyed by stack, then by 'default' or a variant name. Stack/variant key validity against schema/vocab.json is checked by scripts/validate.py, not by this schema. Used by messages/enums; commands use commandCompatibility below instead.

paramStatus.description: compatibility.<stack>.frames.<frame>.params.<key>. Absent param = unknown. A reserved '<index>_Empty' param may only use supported.version_added 'not-applicable' (optional) -- see scripts/validate.py. accept_nan_or_int32max: is this param's sentinel value (NaN for a float-encoded param, INT32_MAX for an int32-encoded one) accepted. nacks_on_non_sentinel_value: is a real (non-sentinel) value correctly rejected -- only meaningful while the param isn't supported. Either may also be set on the enclosing frame as the default for every param without its own.

frameStatus.description: compatibility.<stack>.frames.<frame> for a command doc (context: mission/command only). No 'default' fallback between frames -- every field here is that frame's own explicit fact. params/mav_frames/sentinel subfeatures only valid once some 'supported' range is a real version -- enforced by scripts/validate.py.

params.description: Keyed by '<index>_<name>' matching the sibling definitions doc's params roster. Only the params actually evaluated appear -- an absent param is unknown.

mav_frames.description: Coordinate-frame (MAV_FRAME) support for this vehicle frame -- deliberately a separate key from the vehicle-type 'frames' above, since they're unrelated MAVLink concepts that happen to share an English name.

commandFrames.description: compatibility.<stack>.frames for a command doc. {} = untested, nothing evaluated for any frame yet. false = confirmed unsupported on every frame (a blanket negative fact -- see sibling basis/notes/last_checked_version on the enclosing commandStackStatus). Object = per-frame breakdown keyed by a frame name from schema/vocab.json's frames list for that stack. No 'default' fallback -- absent frame = unknown.

commandStackStatus.description: compatibility.<stack> for a command doc. basis/notes/impl_url/last_checked_version here describe the blanket 'frames: false' case only; when frames is an object each frame carries its own -- enforced by scripts/validate.py, not this schema.

commandCompatibility.description: compatibility for command docs (context: mission/command). Object keyed by stack -> commandStackStatus. Distinct from 'compatibility' above, which messages/enums use (variant-keyed default+override). Stack key validity against schema/vocab.json is checked by scripts/validate.py, not by this schema.
